purpose: Names the frozen US-short governance presets whose contents define the selection and action rules in force. The weekly diagnostic record fingerprints exactly this list so a 26-week report can segment by rule version. Design section 6: the fingerprint is factual metadata, never an input to adjudication, and a rule upgrade segments the report rather than resetting the 26-week clock.
why_a_declared_list: A fingerprint over 'whatever the engine happened to import' is not reviewable and drifts silently. A fingerprint over the weekly decision artifact would change every week and make mixed_ruleset_window permanently true, which destroys the thing section 6 wants it for. So the list is declared here, in a file whose own change is visible in a diff.
why_the_exclusions_are_declared_too: v1.0.0 of this file listed nine presets and silently omitted six that really do define selection and action -- including the core-score weight profile, the single biggest ranking lever. A list with no counterpart is unfalsifiable: nothing could tell it was incomplete. Every preset an engine loads must now be classified as governed or excluded-with-a-reason, so a newly added rule preset fails the guard test instead of being quietly left out.

excluded_presets.presets/us_short_field_registry_governan: field naming and dangling-field registry; changes what a report may say, not what gets picked
excluded_presets.presets/us_short_weekly_report_contract_: section 11.2 report rendering contract; a presentation surface, not a rule
excluded_presets.presets/us_short_market_calendar_2026_20: calendar data, not a decision rule
excluded_presets.presets/us_short_forward_policy_comparis: forward-policy comparison track's own configuration; deliberately isolated from the live rules
excluded_presets.presets/us_short_market_diagnostic_26w_p: this diagnostic track's own policy; already carried separately as diagnostic_policy_sha256

mirrored_authority_note: Two governed entries are frozen authorities the engine mirrors rather than loads at runtime: us_short_hard_veto_governance_20260620.json (ladder hardcoded in engine/us_short_hard_veto.py) and us_short_eligibility_governance_20260624.json (semantics frozen as constants in engine/us_short_eligibility_gate.py, loaded by a runner). They stay governed because a rule upgrade edits the JSON and the mirror together, and the fingerprint is meant to record that the rules changed.
